text: Vessels four grades deep in a rack, with the prices chalked on and re-chalked twice this month.
The largest stock between Stonewake and the water, in a village of four hundred people.
Every bit of it came over the ridge on somebody's back.
Tonics and revives, restocked from a crate that is
still half full on the floor beside the shelf.
The hand keeps meaning to get to it.
Leatherwork, because of course it is. Packs, straps, harness, and boot soles stacked like plates.
It is cured a mile up the lane and it gets into your clothes and travels with you.
The display case runs the whole length of the counter, and one shelf of it is roped off and empty.
The card behind the rope says: RESERVED. FOUNDATION ACCOUNT.
Under it, in the shopkeeper's hand and not meant to be read: THEY PAY ON TIME.
